report.source_text: Endobronchial ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration was done, and the biopsy was taken from the 4R lymph node; a total of 6 specimens were taken. Three specimens were stained with Diff-Quik stain and 3 were prepared unstained. The slides were fixed by Spray-Cyte and sent to the Pathology Laboratory, which showed that the patient’s sample was positive for malignancy, since there were clusters of malignant epithelial cells with enlarged hyperchromatic pleomorphic nuclei with coarse chromatin. Cell-block immunostaining showed positive reactivity of the malignant cells to CK-7, TTF-1, and focally for Napsin-A. These findings indicated primary lung adenocarcinoma.

report.source_text: The patient was admitted to the hospital for a malignancy workup with weakness in the left side of the body. Dexamethasone was started at a loading dose of 10 mg intravenously and continued on a regular dose, and levetiracetam 500 mg orally was started for prophylaxis to prevent convulsions. The patient followed up with the Oncology Department for staging and prognosis. Afterward, the patient was referred to the Palliative Care team.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old Saudi man with a 30-pack-year smoking history presented to the ED with a 2-week history of left-sided weakness (4/5 upper limb, 3/5 lower limb), headache, and constitutional symptoms including unintentional weight loss (6 kg), anorexia, subjective fever, and night sweats. Physical examination revealed clubbed fingers and focal left-sided weakness with intact cranial nerves and normal GCS (15/15). Brain MRI demonstrated 2 ring-enhancing lesions in the right temporal and parietal regions with extensive perifocal edema and midline shift to the left, consistent with brain metastases. CT chest identified a mass in the anterior segment of the right upper lobe, and CT abdomen revealed multiple hypodense liver lesions indicating metastatic disease. Chest X-ray confirmed right lung opacity. EBUS-guided fine-needle aspiration from the 4R lymph node yielded malignant epithelial cells with immunostaining positive for CK-7, TTF-1, and focal Napsin-A, confirming primary lung adenocarcinoma. Laboratory studies (CBC, LFTs, RFTs, amylase, lipase, serum calcium) were within normal limits. The patient was admitted for malignancy workup and initiated on dexamethasone (10 mg IV loading dose, then regular dosing) and levetiracetam 500 mg orally for seizure prophylaxis. The patient was subsequently referred to Oncology for staging and Palliative Care for management of stage IV metastatic disease with brain and liver involvement.
